title: MERCY IN THE MIDDLE OF JUDGEMENT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Give an order now to bring your livestock and everything you have in the field to a place of shelter, because the hail will fall on every person and animal that has not been brought in and is still out in the field, and they will die.'"" - Exodus 9:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse is remarkable. In the middle of announcing the worst hailstorm in Egypt's history, God tells them exactly how to survive it: bring everything under shelter.

He did not have to say that. He is warning the very people who have defied Him, and He is telling them precisely how to be spared.

That is the character of our God. Even His judgements come with instructions for escape. Ezekiel says God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but would rather they turn and live (Ezek 33:11).

The whole Bible follows this pattern. Noah was told to build an ark. Israel was told to put blood on the doorposts. And at the centre of history, God provided the shelter Himself — Christ, in whom there is now no condemnation (Rom 8:1).

The hail was coming for everyone. The only difference was whether you came in when God said come in.

Have you come in?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I taken shelter in Christ, or am I still standing in the field?
2. Whom do I know who needs to hear that shelter is available?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You warn and provide shelter. I take refuge in Christ today. Amen.
